approachQuestion.prompt:
Collect matching three-reading profiles

Input: an array readings of ordered integer triples (a,b,c). Two triples match when some integer d can be added to every coordinate of one to obtain the other; coordinate order matters. Return groups of original indices, one group for each matching class containing at least two indices. Return each qualifying index exactly once. Order within and between groups is unrestricted.

Example 1: readings = [(2,5,9),(10,13,17),(2,9,5),(0,3,7)]. Output: [[0,1,3]]. Example 2: readings = [(1,1,2),(6,6,7),(0,1,1)]. Output: [[0,1]]. Example 3: readings = []. Output: [].

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000. Coordinates lie between −1,000,000,000 and 1,000,000,000; differences use signed 64-bit arithmetic. Keep input unchanged. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Hashing a fixed-size pair of integers has expected amortized constant cost under non-adversarial hashing.

options.text: For each triple at index i, append i to the bucket keyed by the ordered pair (b−a,c−a). Return buckets with at least two indices.
options.feedback: Equal difference pairs are necessary and sufficient: choosing d from the first coordinates then aligns both remaining coordinates. Indices preserve provenance.

options.text: Create records ((b−a,c−a), originalIndex), comparison-sort them by the pair, and group equal neighboring keys.
options.feedback: This retains the complete invariant and original indices, but full comparison sorting adds removable ordering work.

options.text: Group triples by a+b+c and return groups of size at least two.
options.feedback: Matching triples (0,1,2) and (1,2,3) have different totals. Equal totals are also insufficient, as (0,0,3) and (0,1,2) show.

options.text: Use the unordered set {b−a,c−a} as the bucket key.
options.feedback: Triples (2,5,9) and (2,9,5) would collide although no common shift can swap the second and third coordinates.

feedback.reason: Represent an equivalence class by a complete invariant while retaining original indices.
details: Create a map from (b−a,c−a) to a growable list of original indices. Append every index once. Scan all buckets and copy each list of size at least two into the returned result; keep the original bucket lists until the method finishes.
Subtracting the first reading removes a shared translation: (a,b,c) and (a+t,b+t,c+t) have the same two differences. Keep original indices so grouping signatures does not lose provenance.

“For each triple at index i, append i to the bucket keyed by the ordered pair (b−a,c−a). Return buckets with at least two indices.”: Equal difference pairs are necessary and sufficient: choosing d from the first coordinates then aligns both remaining coordinates. Indices preserve provenance.

“Create records ((b−a,c−a), originalIndex), comparison-sort them by the pair, and group equal neighboring keys.”: This retains the complete invariant and original indices, but full comparison sorting adds removable ordering work.
“Group triples by a+b+c and return groups of size at least two.”: Matching triples (0,1,2) and (1,2,3) have different totals. Equal totals are also insufficient, as (0,0,3) and (0,1,2) show.
“Use the unordered set {b−a,c−a} as the bucket key.”: Triples (2,5,9) and (2,9,5) would collide although no common shift can swap the second and third coordinates.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Bucket by an ordered difference pair”, n is the number of triples. Growable-list appends have amortized constant cost. Copying k indices to the result costs O(k) time; the original map and bucket lists remain auxiliary storage. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input of size n, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

feedback.reason: Construct fixed-size signatures and retain bucket indices before copying output.
details: Represent an equivalence class by a complete invariant while retaining original indices.
Each triple produces one constant-size key and one amortized append. The final scan and result copies process at most n indices. Expected O(n + 1).
The map has at most n keys and its retained lists contain n indices even when every class is a singleton. Thus O(n + 1) auxiliary space, excluding the separately copied returned groups.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(n + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(1) auxiliary space.”: Excluding the result does not exclude the retained map and bucket index lists.
“O(n log n + 1) time; O(n + 1) auxiliary space.”: The fixed-size keys are hashed; no comparison sort occurs.
“Expected O(n² + 1) time; O(n + 1) auxiliary space.”: Each triple and stored index is processed a constant number of times; triples are not compared pairwise.
